paper.title: Algorithm 804: Subroutines for the computation of Mathieu functions of integer orders
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 26(3), p. 408 (Sep 2000), per the frame item and the shipped Read.me
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/804.gz (article not fetched; ACM page not used)

code.commit: netlib CALGO archive 804.gz (shell archive; CPP/Dp/Src/*.cpp and *.h, CPP/Dp/Drivers/driver.cpp, Makefile, data1, data2, the reference outputs res1 and res2, and Doc/Read.me)
code.archive: downloaded by scout 2026-11-27 from netlib.org/toms/804.gz (HTTP 200, 34972 bytes). sha256 of 804.gz: d6cb0600a2257bb2f935d370e0d5140a7d57120fafbe39b446fb0fba98b0dd02 (scout download, 2026-11-27).
code.note: Gunzip the archive, then unpack the shell archive with /bin/sh in an empty directory (the shar begins at the #! /bin/sh line). Build CPP/Dp/Drivers with its Makefile (C++), run the driver on data1 (typ e, n 3, circumferential, first kind, standard) and compare its output with the shipped CPP/Dp/Drivers/res1.

claim.location: Shipped reference output CPP/Dp/Drivers/res1 (inside 804.gz). Table row x = 19.790 (degrees; the driver's v = 11 x 0.0314 rad), column 4 (h = 3n = 9), value +2.750024. The driver computes the even circumferential first-kind standard Mathieu function Sn of order 3 with the column's parameter h.

reference.sha256: not computed for the member; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.paper_value: Value +2.750024 at x = 19.790 in column 4 of the shipped res1, as printed by the shipped driver (6 decimals). The paper's table or figure is not read; the claim is the code's own printed output.
claim.metric: The column-4 value of res1 at the row with x = 19.790, compared as an absolute number with the driver's own printed value
claim.determinism: deterministic (fixed data1 input, fixed grid v = k x 0.0314 rad, no random numbers)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The reference is printed to 6 decimals (rounding step 1e-6, so the true printed value lies within 5e-7 of the stored number). 1e-6 allows that rounding plus small libm and compiler differences in the Mathieu series evaluation, while a different algorithm path or a wrong h gives differences in the 1e-3 range or more (neighbouring rows change by about 0.1). Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: one C++ build of the five library sources with the driver and one run on data1.
cost.data_size: None (data1 is five input lines embedded in the shar).
cost.data_licence: Netlib CALGO archive; licence per the archive's own notices and the author's Read.me (the rerun should record it).

why: The shipped driver computes the Mathieu characteristic-function series at a set of parameter values; the value at x = 19.790, h = 9 is a numerical evaluation with no closed form, so the rerun must execute the C++ method to reproduce it.
